prompt:
Task: HD remaster of a sheet of animation frames from the 1995 adventure game The Dig (LucasArts), in the smooth, detailed style approved for the main characters. This is a production asset. Every frame is fitted to the original frame's size and position afterwards, and the game lays it over the HD background with its own soft edges.

Input: the attached image is the original low-resolution sheet enlarged 4x with hard pixel edges. The frames stand apart on a plain flat cyan background (#00C8C8). Around the sheet is a plain gray (#808080) border. The border is only padding.

All frames on this sheet are animation frames of the same characters (Boston Low, Maggie Robbins and Ludger Brink), as one scene, in different poses. On this sheet, row by row from left to right: animation 6, facing right (15 frames).

Do:
- Repaint every frame in high resolution with clean, natural detail: smooth shading instead of dithering, smooth anti-aliased outlines (no pixel steps), believable cloth, skin, hair and material.
- Keep the original look: the same character, the same colors, light direction, shadows and contrast, in the painted style of the approved HD sheets.
- Make all frames look identical apart from the pose: the same face, hair, clothes, colors and light in every frame. The frames are played one after another in the game, so any difference between them flickers.
- Keep the pose, proportions and silhouette of every frame as in the input, and keep each frame in its place on the sheet, in the same rows and the same order.
- Glowing effects (light, energy, lightning, sparks) are painted as soft glow that fades into transparency.

Do not:
- Do not add, remove, merge or redesign frames. Do not add anything between the frames: no shadows, floor, text, numbers, labels, frames or grid lines.
- Do not let frames touch or overlap each other.
- Some frames show only part of the character, for example a body without a head or a head alone, because the game draws the parts separately. Paint them as they are and do not complete them.
- Small bright magenta marks under the feet or at the edges are shadow markers used by the game. Leave them out; the game draws the shadow itself.
- No photorealism, no modern 3D look, no film grain, no vignette, no watermark, no signature.

Output: one PNG image, exactly 1536 x 1024 pixels, with a fully transparent background (real alpha, no background color and no gray border) and the frames in the same layout as the input. List the delivery with its sha256 in the fremdrift.json of your report and add a rutekart (the box around each frame's drawing) as for the main characters.

If a second image is attached, it is an already approved HD sheet of the same character, or an approved HD picture from the same game. Paint the character exactly as in that image: the same face, hair, clothes, colors and level of detail. Take all poses and the layout from the first image.


TOM-AUTHORIZED SOURCE-FAITHFUL IDENTITY CORRECTION, 10 OCTOBER2026. Use case: style-transfer.
Image ONE is the exact original sprite sheet and controls the actual pose, view, clothing, palette, silhouette, incomplete parts, scene composition and row order in EVERY cell. Image TWO is ONLY Ludger Brink's approved face identity: lean older male scientist with long narrow angular face, long straight nose, narrow chin and muted straw-blond hair. Image THREE is ONLY Boston Low's approved face: a man in his fifties, square jaw, short brown top hair and gray temples. Image FOUR is ONLY Maggie's unretouched original game-concept face for her distinct adult female identity and short black bob; it is not a new approved sprite-style sample. Use the smooth drawn finish of approved Boston/Brink face crops across this sheet. Never copy the crops' background, body poses, costumes or composition.
MIXED CHARACTERS: preserve each source character separately. Brink remains the blond man in the gray open jacket and dark navy shirt. Boston remains the brown/gray-haired man in navy short sleeves. Maggie remains the dark-haired woman in the orange jumpsuit with white neckline. Source clothing rust RGB187,71,0,155,55,11 and119,39,0 is authoritative; do not impose the darker damaged costume016 palette or introduce its clothing rips. Brink and Maggie have tiny dark VIOLET RECTANGULAR fabric chest patches ONLY where source-visible, on the exact source viewer-side of their own jacket/jumpsuit. Even a single original violet pixel is meaningful: keep that small foreshortened patch. No round blue pins, no missing or extra emblems. Boston has no invented badge.
Follow actual source heads rather than the generic direction labels. Boston often shows his back/back-three-quarter body and later leans backward with raised arms; never replace these source views with the portrait crop's side pose. Brink and Maggie must keep every original gesture. Talking changes only mouth/jaw: lock skull, hair, neck and head scale within one viewing direction. Do not complete headless bodies, partial limbs or small source pieces into full figures. Some original cells contain two people touching: preserve them as the same complete composite cell with exact internal size and position.
The thin irregular DARK BURGUNDY source shapes extending LEFT from Boston are authentic source parts, including color RGB79,15,55. Preserve their exact narrow contour, loops and connections in each cell. They are NOT the bright magenta shadow markers and must NOT be erased as a floor/shadow/stray artifact. White/light energy where present must also remain in its exact source pose and size, smooth with true alpha, not a new beam or atmosphere. Tiny genuine dark fragments remain tiny. Only bright magenta game shadow-marker pixels are omitted.
Use precisely the original page layout, same rows/ordering and free space. Do not fill unused canvas by enlarging, centering or rearranging people. Exactly1536x1024 RGBA with truly transparent background and smooth edges. No cyan/gray field/border, no floor/cast shadow, no added text/labels/grid/watermark or stray dots.

EXACT MAIN ROWS [5, 5, 5] = 15 source cells. 0 technical one/few-pixel fragments are not extra full figures. They remain original-fallback parts, do not enlarge them.
Row 1: exactly 5 main source cells. 
Row 2: exactly 5 main source cells. 
Row 3: exactly 5 main source cells. 

ACTUAL SOURCE IDENTITY FOR THIS SHEET: the human drawings are ONLY Boston Low in navy short sleeves and rust-orange trousers, with short brown hair and gray temples. No Brink and no Maggie are present. Preserve every actual lean, walk, stand and arm gesture. Image THREE is Boston identity only; do not borrow other portraits' blond hair, gray jacket or feminine features. Burgundy loop and white energy retain source contour and exact relative placement. Tiny native fragments are not new figures.
